plan.english: Boy, listen to my words. When it grows bright, stand up and yoke the two oxen. Put the yoke on their shoulders. Then lead them into the field. The oxen draw the plough, and you keep it straight. Do not strike the oxen; speak to them. A beaten ox quickly grows tired. When the sun is above, give the oxen water. He who guards his own oxen eats his own grain.

clauses.english: Boy, listen to my words.
When it grows bright, stand up and yoke the two oxen.
Put the yoke on their shoulders.
Then lead them into the field.
The oxen draw the plough, and you keep it straight.
Do not strike the oxen; speak to them.
A beaten ox quickly grows tired.
When the sun is above, give the oxen water.
He who guards his own oxen eats his own grain.

plan.english: Son, listen; I have seen many winters. When the frost melts and the earth grows moist, then plough. Do not plough a field that is dry. In dry earth the plough breaks. Plough the whole field three times. Then the seed lies in the earth and grows. A ploughed field gives much grain. Remember these words, son.

clauses.english: Son, listen; I have seen many winters.
When the frost melts and the earth grows moist, then plough.
Do not plough a field that is dry.
In dry earth the plough breaks.
Plough the whole field three times.
Then the seed lies in the earth and grows.
A ploughed field gives much grain.
Remember these words, son.

plan.english: Carry the seed into the field early. Walk through the ploughed field and scatter the seed. Cover the seed with earth. If the seed lies on the earth, the wild beasts eat it. When it has rained, sow. Water nourishes the seed, and the sun ripens the grain. As many seeds as you sow, so many ears grow.

clauses.english: Carry the seed into the field early.
Walk through the ploughed field and scatter the seed.
Cover the seed with earth.
If the seed lies on the earth, the wild beasts eat it.
When it has rained, sow.
Water nourishes the seed, and the sun ripens the grain.
As many seeds as you sow, so many ears grow.

plan.english: Daughter, rise early; the night is leaving. Go to the hearth and look at the fire. If the fire has gone out, bring dry twigs. Lay them on the hearth and give the fire your breath. Then the fire grows strong and burns. Fire warms the house. Guard the fire through the night. A fireless house grows cold.

clauses.english: Daughter, rise early; the night is leaving.
Go to the hearth and look at the fire.
If the fire has gone out, bring dry twigs.
Lay them on the hearth and give the fire your breath.
Then the fire grows strong and burns.
Fire warms the house.
Guard the fire through the night.
A fireless house grows cold.

plan.english: Daughter, bring water into the house. Put the grain in the water and set it on the fire. When the water boils, the grain cooks. Do not leave the hearth. If the grain burns, your father grows angry. When it has become tasty, give it to the men. They come hungry from the field.

clauses.english: Daughter, bring water into the house.
Put the grain in the water and set it on the fire.
When the water boils, the grain cooks.
Do not leave the hearth.
If the grain burns, your father grows angry.
When it has become tasty, give it to the men.
They come hungry from the field.

plan.english: Dawn shone, and the master of the house rose. He yoked the two oxen and led them to the field. His son carried the seed. The oxen drew the plough through the earth. The master ploughed and the son sowed. When the sun was above, they sat down under an oak. They ate and drank water. When it grew dark, the two went home.

clauses.english: Dawn shone, and the master of the house rose.
He yoked the two oxen and led them to the field.
His son carried the seed.
The oxen drew the plough through the earth.
The master ploughed and the son sowed.
When the sun was above, they sat down under an oak.
They ate and drank water.
When it grew dark, the two went home.

plan.english: The field was dry, and the seed did not grow. The master of the house looked at the sky and spoke: "Father Sky, give water to the field!" In the night it rained. Early the earth grew moist, and the seed grew. The master rejoiced and praised Father Sky.

clauses.english: The field was dry, and the seed did not grow.
The master of the house looked at the sky and spoke:
"Father Sky, give water to the field!"
In the night it rained.
Early the earth grew moist, and the seed grew.
The master rejoiced and praised Father Sky.

plan.english: Daughter, winter is coming. Carry the wool into the house and keep it safe. Your brother is bringing branches from the oaks. Lay them by the hearth; the fire dries them. When it grows cold, clothe yourself in wool. Winter does not enter a house in which the fire burns.

clauses.english: Daughter, winter is coming.
Carry the wool into the house and keep it safe.
Your brother is bringing branches from the oaks.
Lay them by the hearth; the fire dries them.
When it grows cold, clothe yourself in wool.
Winter does not enter a house in which the fire burns.

plan.english: Hear me, young man: do not eat up the whole grain. Set aside the good grain for seed. Hide it from the worms. He who eats his own seed in winter, he does not sow. And the house of him who does not sow is hungry. Remember this, and may your children live.

clauses.english: Hear me, young man: do not eat up the whole grain.
Set aside the good grain for seed.
Hide it from the worms.
He who eats his own seed in winter, he does not sow.
And the house of him who does not sow is hungry.
Remember this, and may your children live.

plan.english: The sun ripened the wheat in the field. The ears swelled. Early the men went into the field. They cut off the ears and carried them home. The wives dried the grain in the sun. The boys sang in the field. When it grew dark, the master gave the servants their wage. Then they ate and were sated.

clauses.english: The sun ripened the wheat in the field.
The ears swelled.
Early the men went into the field.
They cut off the ears and carried them home.
The wives dried the grain in the sun.
The boys sang in the field.
When it grew dark, the master gave the servants their wage.
Then they ate and were sated.

plan.english: Listen, boy: I am the cook of this house. I heat the water and put the grain in it. The fire cooks; the cook stays awake. The cook who is not awake, he burns the grain. When the grain has become tasty, carry it to the master. When the master is sated, then eat.

clauses.english: Listen, boy: I am the cook of this house.
I heat the water and put the grain in it.
The fire cooks; the cook stays awake.
The cook who is not awake, he burns the grain.
When the grain has become tasty, carry it to the master.
When the master is sated, then eat.

plan.english: Daughter, the cows are lowing. Go out and milk them. Sing to them, and they stand still. A cow that trembles with fear gives nothing. Then drive the cows to the pasture, and the dog guards them. When it grows dark, the wolf comes. Then lead them home.

clauses.english: Daughter, the cows are lowing.
Go out and milk them.
Sing to them, and they stand still.
A cow that trembles with fear gives nothing.
Then drive the cows to the pasture, and the dog guards them.
When it grows dark, the wolf comes.
Then lead them home.

title: The ox that would not rise

plan.english: The ox lay in the field and did not rise. The boy struck it, and it did not rise. Then Kindly, the master, came. He said: "Do not strike the ox. It is thirsty." The boy brought water, and the ox drank. Then it stood up and drew the plough. And the boy learned.

clauses.english: The ox lay in the field and did not rise.
The boy struck it, and it did not rise.
Then Kindly, the master, came.
He said: "Do not strike the ox.
It is thirsty."
The boy brought water, and the ox drank.
Then it stood up and drew the plough.
And the boy learned.

plan.english: The wheel of the sun turns, and our work turns with it. When the frost melts, plough. When the earth grows warm, sow. When the sun has ripened the grain, cut off the ears. When winter comes, sit down at the hearth and eat your own grain. This is the work of a free man.

clauses.english: The wheel of the sun turns, and our work turns with it.
When the frost melts, plough.
When the earth grows warm, sow.
When the sun has ripened the grain, cut off the ears.
When winter comes, sit down at the hearth and eat your own grain.
This is the work of a free man.

plan.english: When it was growing dark, a guest came to the house. The mistress of the house led him to the hearth. She said: "Dear guest, sit down and be well." Her daughter cooked grain and brought it to him. The guest ate and was sated. He praised the mistress: "May the gods give you good things."

clauses.english: When it was growing dark, a guest came to the house.
The mistress of the house led him to the hearth.
She said: "Dear guest, sit down and be well."
Her daughter cooked grain and brought it to him.
The guest ate and was sated.
He praised the mistress:
"May the gods give you good things."

plan.english: Young man, make the plough out of oak. The pine breaks; the oak stands. Make it straight, and join the plough and the yoke. If the plough breaks in the field, the work lies still. So look at your plough at night and at dawn.

clauses.english: Young man, make the plough out of oak.
The pine breaks; the oak stands.
Make it straight, and join the plough and the yoke.
If the plough breaks in the field, the work lies still.
So look at your plough at night and at dawn.

plan.english: Daughter, when you cook grain, give some to Agni. Agni is the giver of good things. He warms the house and cooks our grain. Speak to him with dear words: "Agni, guard this house, and may you be good to us." My mother told me these things.

clauses.english: Daughter, when you cook grain, give some to Agni.
Agni is the giver of good things.
He warms the house and cooks our grain.
Speak to him with dear words:
"Agni, guard this house, and may you be good to us."
My mother told me these things.

plan.english: It grew dark, and the sheep lay in the field. The shepherd sat by the fire and stayed awake. A wolf crept toward the sheep. The dog heard it and cried out. The shepherd stood up, seized a burning branch, and drove the wolf away. The wolf grew afraid and fled. And the shepherd guarded the sheep through the night.

clauses.english: It grew dark, and the sheep lay in the field.
The shepherd sat by the fire and stayed awake.
A wolf crept toward the sheep.
The dog heard it and cried out.
The shepherd stood up, seized a burning branch, and drove the wolf away.
The wolf grew afraid and fled.
And the shepherd guarded the sheep through the night.

plan.english: When the men bring the ears home, lay them in the sun. The sun dries them. If it rains, carry them inside. Grain that grows moist becomes sour. Then put the dry grain in the house and cover it. So in winter there is grain, and the children are not hungry.

clauses.english: When the men bring the ears home, lay them in the sun.
The sun dries them.
If it rains, carry them inside.
Grain that grows moist becomes sour.
Then put the dry grain in the house and cover it.
So in winter there is grain, and the children are not hungry.

plan.english: There was a servant who did not love work. When the master ploughed, the servant lay under the oak. When the master sowed, the servant ate. Winter came. The master ate his own grain. The servant was hungry. He came to the master's house and sought grain. The master said: "He who does not plough does not eat."

clauses.english: There was a servant who did not love work.
When the master ploughed, the servant lay under the oak.
When the master sowed, the servant ate.
Winter came.
The master ate his own grain.
The servant was hungry.
He came to the master's house and sought grain.
The master said: "He who does not plough does not eat."

plan.english: Young man, look at the sky at dawn. If the sky is red, it will rain; do not sow. If the wind brings frost, cover the seed. When the cattle tremble, Perkwunos is coming. Then lead the cattle home. Your father knows these things; now you too know them.

clauses.english: Young man, look at the sky at dawn.
If the sky is red, it will rain; do not sow.
If the wind brings frost, cover the seed.
When the cattle tremble, Perkwunos is coming.
Then lead the cattle home.
Your father knows these things; now you too know them.

plan.english: Night has come, and the fire burns on the hearth. The mother lays the children down at the hearth. She covers them with wool and sings: "Lie down, children; the dog guards the house. Your father has come from the field; the oxen stand in the shelter. The grain lies in the house; no one is hungry." So she sang, and the mother put them to sleep.

clauses.english: Night has come, and the fire burns on the hearth.
The mother lays the children down at the hearth.
She covers them with wool and sings:
"Lie down, children; the dog guards the house.
Your father has come from the field; the oxen stand in the shelter.
The grain lies in the house; no one is hungry."
So she sang, and the mother put them to sleep.

plan.english: The father took a seed and showed it to his son. "What is in this seed?" said the son. The father said: "An ear and many seeds are in it. Put it in the earth and give it water; then you will see." The son put the seed in the earth. The seed grew and became an ear. The son saw it and rejoiced.

clauses.english: The father took a seed and showed it to his son.
"What is in this seed?" said the son.
The father said: "An ear and many seeds are in it.
Put it in the earth and give it water; then you will see."
The son put the seed in the earth.
The seed grew and became an ear.
The son saw it and rejoiced.

plan.english: Young man, you work for me; I give you a wage. Rise early and go to the field with the oxen. While the sun is in the sky, do not sit down. When it grows dark, come home. Then you eat at our hearth. He who works receives a good wage. He who does not work, him I drive away from my house.

clauses.english: Young man, you work for me; I give you a wage.
Rise early and go to the field with the oxen.
While the sun is in the sky, do not sit down.
When it grows dark, come home.
Then you eat at our hearth.
He who works receives a good wage.
He who does not work, him I drive away from my house.

plan.english: The mistress of the house rose early and spoke to the servants: "You, bring water into the house. You, split branches for the fire. And you, drive the sheep to the pasture. I cook the grain." The servants went out and did their work. When they came back, the mistress gave them grain.

clauses.english: The mistress of the house rose early and spoke to the servants:
"You, bring water into the house.
You, split branches for the fire.
And you, drive the sheep to the pasture.
I cook the grain."
The servants went out and did their work.
When they came back, the mistress gave them grain.

plan.english: When the frost had melted, the master of the house went out to the field. He yoked the oxen and spoke to Earth, the mother: "Mother Earth, receive the seed and nourish it. Give us much grain, and we will praise you." Then he ploughed, and his son sowed. The household sang.

clauses.english: When the frost had melted, the master of the house went out to the field.
He yoked the oxen and spoke to Earth, the mother:
"Mother Earth, receive the seed and nourish it.
Give us much grain, and we will praise you."
Then he ploughed, and his son sowed.
The household sang.

plan.english: Daughter, hear these words about the fire. Do not throw water on the fire. Do not urinate toward the fire or toward the sun. Agni is a god. He sees our deeds. Feed him with dry branches, and he will protect your house.

clauses.english: Daughter, hear these words about the fire.
Do not throw water on the fire.
Do not urinate toward the fire or toward the sun.
Agni is a god.
He sees our deeds.
Feed him with dry branches, and he will protect your house.

plan.english: The father was ploughing in the field. The mother cooked grain and said to her daughter: "Carry this to your father; he is hungry." The daughter and the son went to the field. The father saw them and rejoiced. He ate, and the two sat near him. Then the father ploughed again, and the two went home.

clauses.english: The father was ploughing in the field.
The mother cooked grain and said to her daughter:
"Carry this to your father; he is hungry."
The daughter and the son went to the field.
The father saw them and rejoiced.
He ate, and the two sat near him.
Then the father ploughed again, and the two went home.

plan.english: Son, the seed is the father of the grain. The earth is its mother. The sun warms it; the water nourishes it. And the man who ploughs is the shepherd of the field. Guard the seed, guard the field, guard the oxen. And may your house be filled with grain.

clauses.english: Son, the seed is the father of the grain.
The earth is its mother.
The sun warms it; the water nourishes it.
And the man who ploughs is the shepherd of the field.
Guard the seed, guard the field, guard the oxen.
And may your house be filled with grain.

plan.english: The men went to the pines. They cut off branches and laid them on the earth. When the branches were dry, they burned them. The fire burned, and the wild beasts fled. Then the men ploughed that earth and sowed wheat. That field was fruitful and gave much grain.

clauses.english: The men went to the pines.
They cut off branches and laid them on the earth.
When the branches were dry, they burned them.
The fire burned, and the wild beasts fled.
Then the men ploughed that earth and sowed wheat.
That field was fruitful and gave much grain.

plan.english: Daughter, when a guest comes to our house, lead him to the hearth. Give him water and grain. When he has eaten, then he will tell his own name. The guest is dear to the gods. Whoever drives a guest from his house, the gods strike him down.

clauses.english: Daughter, when a guest comes to our house, lead him to the hearth.
Give him water and grain.
When he has eaten, then he will tell his own name.
The guest is dear to the gods.
Whoever drives a guest from his house, the gods strike him down.

plan.english: Young man, set names on your two oxen. An ox that knows its own name listens to its master. When the oxen arrive at the oak, lead them back. Do not rage at them. Sing to them, and they pull the plough.

clauses.english: Young man, set names on your two oxen.
An ox that knows its own name listens to its master.
When the oxen arrive at the oak, lead them back.
Do not rage at them.
Sing to them, and they pull the plough.

plan.english: The men accomplished their work. The wagons carried the grain to the house. The master filled the house with grain. The cook cooked wheat, and the household ate. They drank and sang and praised the gods: "Gods, givers of good things, give us grain again!"

clauses.english: The men accomplished their work.
The wagons carried the grain to the house.
The master filled the house with grain.
The cook cooked wheat, and the household ate.
They drank and sang and praised the gods:
"Gods, givers of good things, give us grain again!"

plan.english: Daughter, when you go to the house of your husband, cherish his mother and his father. Guard his fire. Rise early and cook the grain. A wife who works fills the house with good things. And her name is famous. These are the words of your mother.

clauses.english: Daughter, when you go to the house of your husband, cherish his mother and his father.
Guard his fire.
Rise early and cook the grain.
A wife who works fills the house with good things.
And her name is famous.
These are the words of your mother.

plan.english: Perkwunos roared in the sky. The cattle trembled and the dogs lay down. The wind broke the ears of grain. The master of the house went out and saw the field. He grew afraid; the grain was lost. But his wife said: "Do not be afraid. We have wheat in the house. We will sow again, and the earth will give again."

clauses.english: Perkwunos roared in the sky.
The cattle trembled and the dogs lay down.
The wind broke the ears of grain.
The master of the house went out and saw the field.
He grew afraid; the grain was lost.
But his wife said: "Do not be afraid.
We have wheat in the house.
We will sow again, and the earth will give again."

plan.english: Young man, the dog is your brother in the field. Feed him. When you lie down, he guards the sheep. When the wolf comes, he cries out. Do not strike the dog; do not drive him from the fire. If the dog is gone, the wolf eats the sheep.

clauses.english: Young man, the dog is your brother in the field.
Feed him.
When you lie down, he guards the sheep.
When the wolf comes, he cries out.
Do not strike the dog; do not drive him from the fire.
If the dog is gone, the wolf eats the sheep.

title: Brother and sister at the hearth

plan.english: "Brother, the fire is not burning; bring branches." "Where are the branches?" "They lie by the shelter." The brother brought branches and laid them on the fire. The fire grew strong, and the sister cooked grain. "Are you hungry, brother?" "I am hungry." "Then sit down and eat." And the two sat down at the hearth and ate the grain.

clauses.english: "Brother, the fire is not burning; bring branches."
"Where are the branches?"
"They lie by the shelter."
The brother brought branches and laid them on the fire.
The fire grew strong, and the sister cooked grain.
"Are you hungry, brother?"
"I am hungry."
"Then sit down and eat."
And the two sat down at the hearth and ate the grain.

plan.english: Young man, do not yoke horses to the plough. The horse is swift; it runs and it tires. The ox does not run, and it does not tire. Yoke the horses to the chariot, the oxen to the plough. The warrior drives horses; the master of the house drives oxen. Do your own work.

clauses.english: Young man, do not yoke horses to the plough.
The horse is swift; it runs and it tires.
The ox does not run, and it does not tire.
Yoke the horses to the chariot, the oxen to the plough.
The warrior drives horses; the master of the house drives oxen.
Do your own work.

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame worked in the master's field. He ploughed, he sowed, he cut off the ears. When the grain was in the house, the master gave him a wage, a measure of wheat. Of-Good-Fame carried the wheat to the house of his own mother. His mother saw him and rejoiced. She said: "My son, you have done good work. May your fame be good."

clauses.english: Of-Good-Fame worked in the master's field.
He ploughed, he sowed, he cut off the ears.
When the grain was in the house, the master gave him a wage, a measure of wheat.
Of-Good-Fame carried the wheat to the house of his own mother.
His mother saw him and rejoiced.
She said: "My son, you have done good work.
May your fame be good."

plan.english: Hear, young man, the words of your fathers. The field feeds the house; the house feeds the field. The plough tears the earth; the seed fills it. From work comes grain, and by grain the house lives. He who lies down at dawn sees no grain in winter. The gods give, and the man works. May the gods give you much grain and good fame.

clauses.english: Hear, young man, the words of your fathers.
The field feeds the house; the house feeds the field.
The plough tears the earth; the seed fills it.
From work comes grain, and by grain the house lives.
He who lies down at dawn sees no grain in winter.
The gods give, and the man works.
May the gods give you much grain and good fame.
